clue.text: Weaken as I provided illumination during exchange of views

indicators.note: during says the following pieces sit within the span of the other word

parts.note: a debate is an exchange of views
lit means provided light, illuminated

explanation.surface: Someone shines a light while a debate goes on, somehow sapping it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange of views' is a long-winded way of describing a debate; 'as' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To debilitate is to sap strength, a direct synonym for weaken.

clue.text: Remove from container and store

definitions.meaning: read as ..., take out of a pot

explanation.definitionFit: Read as de-pot it means take out of a pot, and a depot is a warehouse.

clue.text: Bird a lord fed to dog

indicators.note: fed to means put inside, as food goes into an animal

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A nobleman is given as food to a hound.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a dog being fed a nobleman; 'fed to' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The bald eagle is a North American bird of prey, the US national emblem.

clue.text: Plant producing nothing, having no work

parts.note: love is a score of nothing in tennis
in idleness means without occupation

explanation.surface: A plant fails to yield anything because it has nothing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Love-in-idleness is an old name for the wild pansy, a plant.

clue.text: Terrifying demands make the star collapse

indicators.note: a collapse breaks the words down so their letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Frightening ultimatums might bring down a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Threats are menacing demands meant to frighten someone into compliance.

clue.text: Bar using time and money to obtain one's freedom

parts.note: a ransom is money paid to free a captive

explanation.surface: In a pub, someone pays for their release with time and cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbar, as above a door or window.

clue.text: Missile race

definitions.meaning: to move fast, to race along like clouds

explanation.definitionFit: Scud names a well-known missile and is also a verb for speeding along.

clue.text: Trojan girl refusing local mountain plant

indicators.note: refusing means turning away, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: Cressida is the Trojan heroine of Troilus and Cressida
Mount Ida stands near Troy, local to a Trojan

explanation.surface: A girl from Troy declines to climb a nearby peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Cress is a small salad plant, such as watercress.

clue.text: Colourful coat a problem for pet

definitions.meaning: a coat of water-based paint for walls

explanation.definitionFit: Distemper is both a wall paint and a disease affecting dogs.

clue.text: Slight sign one's hat may have blown away?

definitions.meaning: a small hint of how things are going

definitions.text: one's hat may have blown away?
definitions.meaning: a straw hat caught up by a gust, literally

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a small indication of trends, and literally pictures a straw hat in a gale.

clue.text: With friend, maintain idle conversation

parts.note: a pal is a friend
to aver is to maintain or assert

explanation.surface: Insisting on something alongside a friend turns into pointless chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Palaver is a synonym for lengthy, idle talk or fuss.

clue.text: Natural that Cockney should sound callous

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the initial H, so the word for callous is said in that accent

parts.note: callous means heartless, unfeeling

explanation.surface: A naive person worries that a Londoner's accent makes them seem unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class East Londoner, whose accent famously drops the H at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless means without guile or artifice, so natural and unaffected.

clue.text: Play with keen competitors

definitions.meaning: a comedy of manners by Richard Brinsley Sheridan, first staged in 1775
eager opponents vying with one another

explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan's play has this title, and the phrase literally means a set of competitors.

clue.text: Porter bars one's passage

indicators.note: bars here means encloses, keeping something shut in

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, so a kind of ale
one's is read as one is, I plus IS

explanation.surface: A hotel porter blocks a guest's way through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a hotel worker, but porter is also a dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between rows of seats, as in a church or plane.

clue.text: Singer's line in musical

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the musical's title

parts.note: Gigi is a Lerner and Loewe musical

explanation.surface: A performer delivers a line in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer's' reads as 'Singer is'; L goes inside GIGI.
explanation.definitionFit: Beniamino Gigli was a celebrated Italian operatic tenor, so an example of a singer.

clue.text: Showing amusement as pretentious talk's inspiring respect

parts.note: guff is empty or pretentious talk
awing means filling with awe

explanation.surface: Someone laughs as pompous speech is somehow admired.
explanation.definitionFit: Guffawing is laughing loudly, an obvious show of amusement.

clue.text: Encapsulating one's character in pre-retirement address

definitions.meaning: describing a person's nature in brief, as when you size someone up
the judge's speech to the jury just before it retires to consider its verdict

explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' looks like leaving work, but it is the jury retiring.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means summarising someone, and is also the judge's closing speech to a jury.

clue.text: Arm offered to old band leader proves explosive

parts.note: a gun is a firearm
Billy Cotton was a British dance-band leader of the mid-20th century

explanation.surface: Weapons offered to a veteran bandleader turn out to be dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Cotton led a popular British dance band on radio and TV from the 1930s to the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Guncotton is nitrocellulose, a highly flammable explosive.

clue.text: Not tied to employer, fish in the country

indicators.note: in places the fish inside the name of the country

parts.note: France is the country meant
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Someone fishing abroad is free of any boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance works for themselves, selling services to many clients rather than one employer.

clue.text: Two presents impossible to locate?

parts.note: now is present in time
here is present in place

explanation.surface: Two gifts somehow cannot be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presents' looks like gifts, but means present in time and present in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is nowhere cannot be found anywhere at all.

clue.text: It goes round in one's head

definitions.text: It goes round in one's head

parts.words: It goes round in one's head
parts.note: something spherical that rotates within the skull, not a nagging tune

explanation.definitionFit: The eye's globe is a round organ that swivels in its socket in the head.

clue.text: Purport to show range of 14 across

definitions.meaning: the general drift or meaning of something
the voice range of the singer at 14 across, Gigli

explanation.definitionFit: Tenor means general meaning or gist, and is the voice range Gigli sang in.

clue.text: No god rejected by a high priest

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the two words are read backwards

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A high priest refuses to accept any deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' acts on both words together, so 'No god' read backwards follows the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron, brother of Moses, was the first high priest of the Israelites.

clue.text: Come back to put coin in bank

indicators.note: in places the coin inside the word for bank

parts.note: to bank on is to rely
P stands for penny, a coin

explanation.surface: Return to deposit some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is the verb, as in bank on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To reply is to respond, to come back with an answer.

clue.text: Unhappy, stop speaking and go away

indicators.note: speaking means the word for stop is said out loud

parts.note: whoa is a call meaning stop
begone is an order to go away

explanation.surface: Someone told to stop talking and leave is understandably downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Woebegone describes someone looking sad and miserable, a synonym for unhappy.

clue.text: Cancel Times magazine in the end

parts.note: eras are periods of time

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of magazine

explanation.surface: Scrap The Times magazine eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but means ERAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to delete or wipe out, so to cancel.

clue.text: Unpromising situation where troublemaker takes almost full advantage

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous troublemaker

indicators.note: almost the full word means all but its last letter

parts.note: an asset is an advantage

explanation.surface: A mischief-maker exploits a situation that looks bleak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost full' drops the T from ASSET, leaving ASSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock, a situation where no progress seems possible.

clue.text: From limitless collection, start to trill a number from opera

indicators.note: limitless means losing its first and last letters

parts.note: a variety is a collection of different things

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: From a varied anthology, the opening trill launches an operatic piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An arietta is a short aria, a song or number in an opera.

clue.text: Painter's year in part of India

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the region's name

parts.note: Goa is a state of India

explanation.surface: An artist spends a year in an Indian region.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was a Spanish painter, so an example of one.

clue.text: The voluptuous flaunting of a button?

definitions.text: The voluptuous flaunting of a button?

parts.words: The voluptuous flaunting of a button?
parts.note: the button is the navel, flaunted in a sensual Middle Eastern dance

explanation.definitionFit: This sensuous dance draws attention to the navel, the so-called belly button.
